result.title: Extending FAIR Principles with Observability for Trustworthy Federated Learning
result.comment: The paper has been accepted by TrustFL-SIS 2026 - Trustworthy Federated Learning for Smart Industrial Systems Workshop, co-located with IEEE ICDM 2026,
result.summary: Federated learning (FL) keeps data at its source, but locality alone does not make a federation trustworthy. Without sufficient observability, an aggregator cannot determine whether the client service was healthy, the local data pipeline was trustworthy, or contractual constraints were properly monitored during training. We take the position that trustworthy FL needs an evidence plane in addition to its model-update process. Each participant continuously summarizes local infrastructure, data into minimal, signed trust evidence associated with each FL round, while raw data, logs remain local. A local TinyLLM may assist in interpreting observability signals, deriving contextual evidence, and providing natural-language explanations to operators. We instantiate this vision through FAIR-O, an observability extension of FAIR principle. Rather than benchmarking FL accuracy, a three-level trust model has been proposed and a two-participant Python prototype demonstrates evidence generation and trust assessment. We further discuss future integration of FAIR-O Trust Evidence into participant selection, evidence weighting, and federated aggregation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出在联邦学习中加入可观测性「证据平面」的 FAIR-O 框架：各参与方持续将本地基础设施与数据管线摘要为签名的信任证据，配合三级信任模型，并用双参与方 Python 原型演示证据生成与信任评估，辅以本地 TinyLLM 解释可观测信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文的「证据」指基础设施遥测与合规审计信息，目标是联邦学习的可信治理，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部状态、证据筛选或停止决策，未见可供核查的 LVR 方法线索，故排除。
